newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee firm, RBI inactive, new PM discounted.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee firm, RBI inactive, new PM discounted.

text.p: The Indian rupee firmed against the dollar on Monday.
But despite the appointment of a new prime minister, dealers put the gains down to inaction by the central bank to stop the rupee's rise, rather than the end of a three-week political crisis.
In afternoon trade, the rupee was quoted 35.757/765 per dollar after opening at 35.79/80.
Dealers said the Reserve Bank of India bought June and August delivery dollars in a limited way on Monday.
Earlier, Inder Kumar Gujral was sworn in as successor to H.D. Deve Gowda as Prime Minister, effectively ending fears that the country was headed toward snap polls.
The rupee's recent strength, which has taken it to four month highs, rested on a combination of poor demand from importers and RBI inaction, dealers said.
"There is just no demand for dollars at the moment," said the chief foreign exchange dealer at a European bank.
"Even the RBI has been off the market and this has added to the upward pressure on the rupee," he said.
Dealers said the rupee could climb up to 35.70 if dollar demand did not come into the market soon.
"The 35.75 level could be the major barrier," said one dealer. "If this is broken, then we could see a rapid rise to 35.70."
He said importers were staying away while the rupee gained. Conversely, exporters were selling dollars as they stood to lose from an appreciating rupee.
"The rupee's rise was checked only by expectations of RBI intervention," said another dealer. "Otherwise there has been very little demand for dollars from corporates."
"But now even the RBI is keeping off...It appears it is more worried about the effect its intervention has on domestic monetary supply growth."
RBI dollar purchases inject rupees into the banking system contributing to money supply expansion. Excessive money supply growth stokes inflationary pressures.
The RBI has targeted an M3 growth rate of 15.0-15.5 percent for 1997/98 (April-March) to keep inflation around 6.0 percent.
Year-on-year inflation as measured by the wholesale price index was 6.99 for the week ended April 5, 1997 against 5.23 percent last year.
Last year, M3 grew by 15.6 percent.
